title: Float oxygen on sigma0 26.5 at 25-46 N, 130-160 W stayed 15-34 umol/kg below 1984-1996 in 2006-2015, as the 10-year-lag source model of the CalCOFI low requires (BGC-Argo, offset corrected)
abstract: Question: a campaign study linked the 2009-2025 oxygen low on sigma0 26.5 off southern California (CalCOFI) to an earlier loss in the offshore transition zone and eastern gyre (25-46 N, 130-160 W), with a lag model CalCOFI(t) = 0.779 U(t - 10) fitted to 22 ship cruises. We tested it out of sample with BGC-Argo floats. Since CalCOFI stayed low in 2016-2025, the model requires an upstream change of about -16 umol/kg in 2006-2015. Approach: 46,738 float profiles from 355 floats (2006-2026). For each profile we calculated the oxygen change from the 1984-1996 GLODAP state of the same water type (salinity on the isopycnal) at casts within 200 km. We corrected floats with a crossover offset from 603 float-ship matches (50 km, 10 days). The plan was written before float oxygen was calculated. Results: floats read 5.8 umol/kg (2.9 to 8.6), or 3.3%, lower than bottles. After correction, the 2006-2015 upstream change was -18.1 umol/kg (13 floats); the difference from the requirement was -2.0 (-4.8 to +1.0). In eight method variants the change was -15.1 to -34.1, so the source never recovered. GLODAP cruises gave -16.2 (1997-2008) and -19.9 (2009-2015). In 2016-2026 the change was -23.9 (26 floats), so the model forecasts a CalCOFI within-type anomaly of -18.6 (variants -15.8 to -24.6) for 2026-2036, against -12.6 in 2016-2025. Floats near California reproduced the CalCOFI low (-12.5). A refit with the extended index gave a lag of 12 years (bootstrap 0-14). The loss was 12-26 umol/kg in water with 1984-1996 AOU of 20-140 but 0-8 at AOU 140-220; a loss proportional to AOU (uniform fractional respiration increase) predicts -50 there against -4 observed, in float and ship data. Limitations: the exact agreement needs the float offset (uncorrected: 7.7 below the requirement); offsets differ by calibration class; few floats before 2011; the reference comes from few ship lines; a subarctic check against Line P was inconclusive; the AOU test pools pathways and does not separate ventilation from a respiration change in young water. Record-level source data stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Within-water-type oxygen change on sigma0 26.5 from 1984-1996 in the transition zone and eastern gyre (TZ+GYR). Orange: the upstream state that the lag model requires, CalCOFI(t+10)/0.779. Black symbols: GLODAP ship cruises. Blue: BGC-Argo annual means after the crossover offset, with a float-bootstrap 95% interval. Shaded boxes: range of 8 method variants for 2006-2015 and 2016-2026; thick bars: main estimates. Gray dashed: CalCOFI within-type series in its own year.

A: float minus ship oxygen on sigma0 26.5 for match windows of 30 km/5 days to 150 km/30 days, by float calibration class (mean of float means, 95% float bootstrap). B: oxygen change from 1984-1996 against the 1984-1996 AOU of the same water type, for floats (2011-2026) and GLODAP casts (2009-2021); dotted lines: a loss proportional to AOU fitted at AOU 20-100.

Float-year mean oxygen change on sigma0 26.5 in 2016-2026 relative to the 1984-1996 ship state (local water-type reference within 200 km, offset corrected). Gray dots: 1984-1996 GLODAP reference casts. Boxes: analysis regions; dashed box: CalCOFI grid.
